entry_label: GOVERNMENT PUBLIC NOTICE — GREATER BENGALURU AUTHORITY
title: Greater Bengaluru Authority — Vacant Site Owners Directed to Clear Waste and Debris
authority: Greater Bengaluru Authority (Office of the Chief Commissioner)
status: Official Public Notice as issued by GBA Chief Commissioner
what_was_issued:
With the objective of keeping Bengaluru city clean, beautiful, and livable, the "Freedom from Waste" campaign is being conducted during August-2026. As per bye-law 18(1)(b) of the Solid Waste Management Bye-laws, 2020, it is the mandatory responsibility of owners to maintain vacant sites in a clean and hygienic condition.

Accordingly, the following directions are issued to the general public with respect to the cleaning of vacant sites:
1. Owners of vacant sites within the GBA limits shall ensure that all waste, garbage, and debris accumulated on their vacant site/s are removed on or before 15.08.2026. The waste/debris shall be disposed of only at the designated disposal locations identified & already notified by the Municipal Corporation. If necessary, owners may also avail the services of agencies notified by the respective Municipal Corporation for cleaning and disposal.
2. If the owners fail to clean their vacant sites by 15.08.2026, the Municipal Corporation will undertake the removal of the waste/debris. The expenditure incurred will be recovered as shown in the table from the property owners along with property tax in accordance with bye-law 18(1)(d)(ii) of the Solid Waste Management Bye-laws, 2020 and Section 285(2) of the Greater Bengaluru Administration Act, 2024.
rule_behind_it: Bye-law 18(1)(b) & Bye-law 18(1)(d)(ii) of the Solid Waste Management Bye-laws, 2020 and Section 285(2) of the Greater Bengaluru Administration Act, 2024.
consequences: If vacant sites are not cleared, the Municipal Corporation will undertake removal of waste/debris and the expenditure incurred will be recovered directly from property owners alongside property tax.
rates_note: In case site dimension/area exceeds above limit, expenditure proportionate to the site area will be recovered.
